\n \n

耶稣又设一个比喻，对他们说：“你们看无花果树和各样的树；它们一发芽，你们看见了，自然就知道夏天近了。照样，你们看见这些事发生，也就知道　神的国近了。”——路加福音 21:29-31。

\n

夏天确实已经来到，树木也已发芽。对现代英语来说，这是个多么有意思的说法；不过，我们仍然明白它的意思，也能在脑海中想象正在发生的事——叶子从那些整个冬天光秃秃的地方冒出来。我想，对我来说，这幅景象更容易想象，因为我看过植物生长或萌芽的延时视频。

\n

不管怎么说，这些先说到这里。经文的其余部分呢？（……你们看见这些事发生，也就知道　神的国近了。）我们大多数人肯定仍看见末日渐渐临近——战争和战争的风声、地震、一个又一个国家的政治动荡、社会离　神越来越远，以及教会和家庭遭罪恶与丑闻蹂躏。

\n

我们有上帝亲自赐下的应许：我们在这地上所知道和经历的一切，都是祂设计、创造并预定为暂时的现实。又说：主啊，你起初立了地的根基；天也是你手所造的。 天地都要灭没，你却要长存。天地都要像衣服渐渐旧了； 你要将天地卷起来，像一件外衣，天地就都改变了。惟有你永不改变；你的年数没有穷尽。——希伯来书 1:10-12。

\n

疑惑与恐惧这一挥之不去的威胁

\n

当我们作为一个教会（FCF）和一个事工（TBV），面对种种艰难处境（破裂的家庭、陷入困境的婚姻、被收养的孩子、信心动摇的年轻人、不道德的成瘾行为、情绪困扰和心理健康问题）时，我们一再遇到疑惑的问题：“为什么这事发生在我身上？”“为什么　神不改变我的处境？”“这些痛苦的事都发生在我身上，我怎么能信靠　神？”“祂既不可信，我怎么能把生命交托给　神？”

\n

大多数信徒都声称信靠　神、相信祂的话语。我们每个人似乎都会面对双重挑战。第一，我们许多人往往以为，相信主要是“感觉”，而不是“选择”。第二，当　神所说的话与我们的经历、思想和感受一致时，我们许多人很容易相信；问题出现在圣经的话触及我的意志、看法、信念、经历等时。

\n

关于第一点（相信＝感觉），使徒保罗给了我们　神清楚的回答：因我们行事为人是凭着信心，不是凭着眼见。——哥林多后书 5:7。关于第二点，事实是，这些挣扎无一不是明确的考验：我们是否会顺服　神而不顺服人（包括我们自己），是否会让　神成为真实的，让人人都成为说谎的（包括我们自己），以及我们是否会让　神在万事上作权威，还是仍坚持自己的意愿。我们许多人嘴上声称（只是口头表示）凡事都信靠、相信　神，可当我们面临自己的考验时，却一败涂地（我知道我自己就曾如此）。

\n

此外，我们许多人把自己充满疑虑和忧虑的生活方式看作正常，但圣经告诉我们不要忧虑任何事，并要把一切忧虑卸给主。在这方面，世俗观念渐渐使我们对圣经清楚的教导麻木，以至于我们开始把　神要我们胜过的事视为正常。如果我们退一步，把“恐惧”看作一个程度不一的范围——有些恐惧很轻微，有些则相当严重——就会看见，我们许多被视为理所当然的行为模式，都偏离了　神对我们生命的完全旨意。疑惑处在这个范围较轻的一端，忧虑的影响稍强一些，而惊慌或手足无措显然会更严重地干扰我们的正常生活。然而，事实是，这些情形仍都属于“恐惧”这一类；结果就是，我们任由恐惧控制我们，支配我们的思想和行为。　神的旨意是让祂所有的儿女凭信心而行，不凭恐惧而行。

\n

　神从不为我们的忧虑，也不为未来种种可能发生的“万一”赐下恩典。　神只赐我们恩典，使我们一刻一刻地经历祂摆在我们面前的事。正如怀孕的妇女必须面对分娩疼痛可能带来的可怕情形，同样，所有人都必须经历　神所定、落在我们生命中的每一种处境。无论我们试图怎么想或怎么做（害怕、忧虑、搬家、改变住处、花钱或请别人介入等），都不能阻止或改变　神对我们生命的旨意。我们可以选择接受或抗拒生命中无法避免的事。

\n

事实是，我们每个人要么会把自己的肢体献给罪，作不义的器具，相信撒但的谎言，继续任由恐惧驱使并引导我们的思想和行动；要么会把自己献给　神，像从死里复活的人一样，并把肢体献给　神，作义的器具（罗马书 6:13），选择相信　神在祂话语中所说的，并让信心驱使和引导我们的思想和行动。

\n

这里需要一个平衡的看法。这并不意味着我们从不与艰难处境搏斗——耶稣在客西马尼园也曾如此。这也不意味着我们从不恳求　神或我们的掌权者考虑改变眼下痛苦的处境——耶稣也曾如此。相反，我们应当向　神坦诚（像耶稣那样），承认内心的挣扎；但最终，我们需要凭信心、带着勇气，继续顺服前行（像耶稣那样）。

\n

And he [Jesus] spake to them a parable; Behold the fig tree, and all the trees; When they now shoot forth, ye see and know of your own selves that summer is now nigh at hand. So likewise ye, when ye see these things come to pass, know ye that the kingdom of God is nigh at hand –Luk 21:29-31.

Summer truly is upon us; and the trees have shot forth. What an interesting term for our modern-day English language, yet we still understand its meaning and have a mental picture of what is happening—the leaves pushing out from places that over winter were bare. For me, I think it is easier to have this mental picture since I have seen time-lapse videos of plants growing or sprouting to life.

Anyway, so much for that. What about the rest of this verse? (…when ye see these things come to pass, know ye that the kingdom of God is nigh at hand.) Surely most of us continue to see the end of time approaching—the wars and rumors of wars, the earthquakes, the political upheaval in nation after nation, societies moving further and further away from God, and churches and families being ravished by sin and scandal.

We have God’s own promise that what we know and experience here on this earth was designed, created, and expected by Him to be only a temporary reality. And, Thou, Lord, in the beginning hast laid the foundation of the earth; and the heavens are the works of thine hands: They shall perish; but thou remainest; and they all shall wax old as doth a garment; And as a vesture shalt thou fold them up, and they shall be changed: but thou art the same, and thy years shall not fail –Heb 1:10-12.

The Prevailing Menace of Doubt & Fear

As we, as a church (FCF) and as a ministry (TBV), interact with numerous challenging situations (broken homes, struggling marriages, adopted children, faltering youth, immoral addictions, emotional struggles, and mental health issues) we repeatedly run into questions of doubt. “Why did this happen to me?” “Why doesn’t God change my circumstances?” “How can I trust God when all these painful things have happened to me?” “How can I surrender my life to God when He isn’t trustworthy?”

Most believers claim to trust God and believe His Word. The challenge that seems to come for each of us is two-fold. First, many of us tend to think that believing is primarily “feeling” instead of “choosing.” Secondly, many of us find it easy to believe what God says when it agrees with our experience, our thoughts, and our feelings; the problem arises when what the Scriptures say pushes on my will, my view, my belief, my experience, etc.

On the first point (believing=feeling) we have God’s clear answer from the Apostle Paul, for we walk by faith, not by sight: –2Co 5:7. On the second point the reality is that each of these struggles are a clear test of whether we will obey God rather than man (including ourselves), whether we will let God be true and every man a liar (including ourselves), and whether we will allow God to be the authority on all things or if we will still insist on our own will. Many of us claim (give lip service) to trust and believe God in all things, yet when we are faced with our own time of testing, we fail miserably (I know I have).

Additionally, many of us define our lifestyle of doubts and worry as being something normal, yet the Bible tells us to be anxious for nothing and to cast all our cares upon our Lord. Here the world has slowly deadened our senses to the clear teaching of the Scriptures, in that we have come to accept as normal that which God would have us to rise above. If we step back and consider the definition of “fear” as being on a spectrum, with some fear being quite minor and some being quite severe, we will see that many of our accepted patterns of behavior are outside of God’s perfect will for our lives. Doubt would be on the lesser end of the spectrum, with worry having a slightly stronger presence and effect, while panicking or being frantic would obviously cause much greater interference in our normal lives. Yet the truth is that each one of these is still in the family of “fear,” with the outcome being that we are allowing fear to control us and dictate our thoughts and behaviors. God’s will is that all His children would walk by faith instead of by fear.

God never gives us grace for any of our worries, nor for any future possible “what ifs”. God only gives us grace to go through what He is placing in front of us moment by moment. In the same way that a woman with child must go through the scary possibilities of the pain of childbirth, so likewise, all human beings must go through each circumstance that God decides is our lot in life. Nothing that we try to think or do (fear, worry, move, change our location, spend money, or ask others to intervene, etc.) will stop or change what God wills for our life. It is our choice to either accept or resist the inevitable in our lives.

The reality is this—each of us will either yield [our] members as instruments of unrighteousness unto sin by believing the lies of Satan and continuing to allow fear to motivate and direct our thoughts and actions, OR we will yield [ourself] unto God, as those that are alive from the dead, and our members as instruments of righteousness unto God (Rom 6:13), by choosing to believe what God says in His Word and allowing faith to motivate and direct our thoughts and actions.

Here a balancing perspective needs to be brought in. This does not mean that we never wrestle with difficult situations—Jesus did in the Garden of Gethsemane. It also doesn’t mean that we never appeal to God or our authorities to consider changing our current painful situation—again, Jesus did. Rather, we are to be honest with God (like Jesus was) about the struggle of our heart, but then we need to eventually walk forward in obedience, by faith, with courage (like Jesus did).

Ongoing Support Needed

A big thank you to all who so faithfully continue to support the work of The Berean Voice. It is through the many prayers, emails and phone calls of encouragement and suggestions, and the financial contributions of many believers that we can continue to minister to the needs of others. As a non-profit ministry of the church, we do not charge for our material or services, therefore we rely entirely on the ongoing freewill offerings of God’s people. Please prayerfully consider how God would have you to partner with us in this work.

If you believe that God would have you support us financially, monthly support makes our work easier since most of our bills are monthly. However, if this doesn’t work as well for you that is fine. For your convenience there is a remittance envelope in the center of each copy of the magazine or you can go to our website www.bereanvoice.org and use the “donate” feature there for online donations. Ed egli [Gesù] disse loro una parabola: «Guardate il fico e tutti gli alberi. Quando germogliano, lo vedete e sapete da voi stessi che l’estate è ormai vicina. Così anche voi, quando vedrete accadere queste cose, sappiate che il regno di Dio è vicino» – Lc 21:29-31.

L’estate è davvero arrivata e gli alberi hanno germogliato. È un’espressione interessante per l’inglese moderno, eppure ne comprendiamo ancora il significato e ci formiamo un’immagine mentale di ciò che accade: le foglie che spuntano da rami rimasti spogli durante l’inverno. Per me è più facile immaginarlo perché ho visto video accelerati di piante che crescono o germogliano tornando alla vita.

Comunque, basta così. E il resto di questo versetto? (…quando vedrete accadere queste cose, sappiate che il regno di Dio è vicino.) Sicuramente la maggior parte di noi continua a vedere avvicinarsi la fine dei tempi: le guerre e le voci di guerre, i terremoti, gli sconvolgimenti politici in una nazione dopo l’altra, le società che si allontanano sempre più da Dio e le chiese e le famiglie devastate dal peccato e dagli scandali.

Abbiamo la promessa stessa di Dio che ciò che conosciamo e sperimentiamo qui sulla terra è stato da lui progettato, creato e previsto come una realtà soltanto temporanea. E tu, Signore, nel principio fondasti la terra, ed i cieli son opere delle tue mani. Essi periranno, ma tu dimori; ed invecchieranno tutti, a guisa di vestimento. E tu li piegherai come una vesta, e saranno mutati; ma tu sei sempre lo stesso, e i tuoi anni non verranno giammai meno. – Eb 1:10-12.

La minaccia persistente del dubbio e della paura

Nel nostro impegno, come chiesa (FCF) e come ministero (TBV), ad affrontare numerose situazioni difficili (famiglie distrutte, matrimoni in crisi, figli adottivi, giovani in difficoltà, dipendenze immorali, lotte emotive e problemi di salute mentale), ci imbattiamo ripetutamente in domande dettate dal dubbio. «Perché è successo a me?» «Perché Dio non cambia le mie circostanze?» «Come posso fidarmi di Dio dopo che mi sono accadute tutte queste cose dolorose?» «Come posso affidare la mia vita a Dio se non è degno di fiducia?»

La maggior parte dei credenti afferma di fidarsi di Dio e di credere alla sua Parola. La sfida che sembra presentarsi a ciascuno di noi è duplice. Primo, molti di noi tendono a pensare che credere significhi soprattutto «sentire» invece di «scegliere». Secondo, molti di noi trovano facile credere a ciò che Dio dice quando concorda con la nostra esperienza, i nostri pensieri e i nostri sentimenti; il problema sorge quando ciò che dicono le Scritture mette in discussione la mia volontà, il mio punto di vista, le mie convinzioni, la mia esperienza e così via.

Sul primo punto (credere = sentire), abbiamo la chiara risposta di Dio per mezzo dell’apostolo Paolo: camminiamo per fede, non per visione – 2 Co 5:7. Quanto al secondo punto, la realtà è che ciascuna di queste lotte è una chiara prova per stabilire se ubbidiremo a Dio anziché agli uomini (noi stessi compresi), se lasceremo che Dio sia verace e ogni uomo bugiardo (noi stessi compresi) e se permetteremo a Dio di essere l’autorità su ogni cosa oppure continueremo a insistere sulla nostra volontà. Molti di noi affermano (a parole) di fidarsi di Dio e di credere in lui in ogni cosa, eppure, quando affrontiamo il nostro momento di prova, falliamo miseramente (so che è capitato a me).

Inoltre, molti di noi definiscono il proprio stile di vita fatto di dubbi e preoccupazioni come qualcosa di normale, eppure la Bibbia ci dice di non essere in ansia per nulla e di gettare ogni nostra preoccupazione sul Signore. A poco a poco, il mondo ha reso ottusi i nostri sensi di fronte al chiaro insegnamento delle Scritture, tanto che abbiamo finito per accettare come normale ciò al di sopra del quale Dio vorrebbe che ci elevassimo. Se ci fermiamo a considerare la «paura» come uno spettro, con forme piuttosto lievi e altre molto gravi, vedremo che molti dei comportamenti che abbiamo accettato esulano dalla perfetta volontà di Dio per la nostra vita. Il dubbio si troverebbe all’estremità più lieve dello spettro, la preoccupazione avrebbe una presenza e un effetto leggermente più forti, mentre farsi prendere dal panico o essere in preda alla frenesia provocherebbe ovviamente un’interferenza molto maggiore nella nostra vita quotidiana. La verità, tuttavia, è che tutte queste cose appartengono ancora alla famiglia della «paura»: il risultato è che permettiamo alla paura di controllarci e di dettare i nostri pensieri e comportamenti. La volontà di Dio è che tutti i suoi figli camminino per fede anziché per paura.

Dio non ci dà mai la grazia per nessuna delle nostre preoccupazioni, né per i possibili «e se…» del futuro. Dio ci dà la grazia soltanto per affrontare, momento per momento, ciò che mette davanti a noi. Come una donna incinta deve affrontare le spaventose possibilità del dolore del parto, così tutti gli esseri umani devono attraversare ogni circostanza che Dio stabilisce essere la sorte della loro vita. Nulla di ciò che tentiamo di pensare o fare (avere paura, preoccuparci, trasferirci, cambiare luogo, spendere denaro o chiedere ad altri di intervenire, ecc.) fermerà o cambierà ciò che Dio vuole per la nostra vita. Sta a noi scegliere se accettare o resistere all’inevitabile nella nostra vita.

La realtà è questa: ciascuno di noi o cede le proprie membra al peccato, come strumenti d’iniquità, credendo alle menzogne di Satana e continuando a permettere che la paura motivi e diriga i nostri pensieri e le nostre azioni, OPPURE si offre a Dio, come chi è stato vivificato dai morti, e offre le proprie membra a Dio come strumenti di giustizia (Rm 6:13), scegliendo di credere a ciò che Dio dice nella sua Parola e permettendo alla fede di motivare e dirigere i nostri pensieri e le nostre azioni.

È necessario introdurre qui una prospettiva equilibrata. Questo non significa che non lottiamo mai con situazioni difficili: Gesù lo fece nel giardino del Getsemani. E non significa neppure che non chiediamo mai a Dio o alle autorità di prendere in considerazione un cambiamento della nostra attuale situazione dolorosa: anche Gesù lo fece. Piuttosto, dobbiamo essere sinceri con Dio (come lo fu Gesù) riguardo alla lotta del nostro cuore, ma poi dobbiamo infine andare avanti nell’ubbidienza, per fede e con coraggio (come fece Gesù).

È necessario un sostegno costante

Un grande ringraziamento a tutti coloro che continuano fedelmente a sostenere l’opera di The Berean Voice. È grazie alle numerose preghiere, alle e-mail e alle telefonate di incoraggiamento e di suggerimenti, e ai contributi finanziari di tanti credenti, che possiamo continuare a servire chi è nel bisogno. In quanto ministero non profit della chiesa, non facciamo pagare i nostri materiali o servizi; perciò dipendiamo interamente dalle offerte volontarie continuative del popolo di Dio. Vi invitiamo a considerare in preghiera in che modo Dio vorrebbe che collaboraste con noi in quest’opera.

Se credete che Dio voglia che ci sosteniate finanziariamente, il sostegno mensile ci facilita il lavoro, poiché la maggior parte delle nostre spese è mensile. Tuttavia, se per voi non è altrettanto pratico, va benissimo lo stesso. Per vostra comodità, al centro di ogni copia della rivista troverete una busta per le offerte; oppure potete visitare il nostro sito www.bereanvoice.org e usare la funzione «donate» per fare una donazione online. Di seguito trovate una stima delle nostre necessità, perché possiate prenderla in considerazione.

Children, obey your parents in all things: for this is well pleasing unto the Lord –Col 3:20.

Years ago, there was a boy named Joey who lived with his father and mother on the outskirts of a city. One day Joey’s father gave him a brand new red and white bike, which he had been wanting for a long time.

There was a big hill close to their house where the big boys in the neighborhood enjoyed riding their bikes. Joey’s father strictly forbade him from riding with the big boys on the hill, since it was too dangerous. Instead, he was only allowed to ride down the nice smooth sidewalk, past numerous houses, through a little alley, and then finally back to his house once again.

As the days and weeks went by, this began to lose its excitement. He watched enviously as the big boys walked their bikes up the hill almost directly in front of his house. At the top they would jump on their bikes, and with gleeful shouts, race down the hardtop road, swiftly turning onto the adjoining street at the bottom of the hill.

“Whee, here we come!” they would shout as they rushed by, leaving Joey to pedal calmly on around his little block again and again.

“Come on Joey!” the boys hollered. “Why don’t you come up with us? See what fun we are having! You are too scared,” they teased.

Joey was too embarrassed to tell them that his father had forbidden him since he was too little and might fall off his bike and hurt himself. The boys would have only made more fun of him, so he remained silent. How he wished he could go up and show his friends that he was not afraid. Joey thought, “Maybe if I would go down the hill just once, my dad would realize that I’m not so little after all. Then Dad would be proud of me and let me go down the hill with the big boys anytime I want to. Oh, how exciting that would be.” The very thought made his heart beat quickly in anticipation.

Joey did not need to wait very long for his opportunity. His father was going to be gone for a couple of days on business. Joey thought this would be his chance to prove to his dad that he was able to ride his bike with the big boys. With excitement and anticipation, he took his bike up the hill. He felt so grown-up in the big boys’ company. Surely his father was wrong! Now he would prove to everybody that he knew better than anyone else what he was able to do and not do.

With a run and a hop, he was on his bike. As the bike went faster and faster, he grabbed the handlebars more firmly. At that moment, one of the mischievous boys, coming up the hill, tossed a stone at Joey’s tire as he flew by. Joey swerved sharply to avoid the stone. Before he knew what was happening, he was sailing thru the air without his bike. He rolled and skidded and bumped, before coming to a painful stop. Joey was one big mess. His pants and shirt were torn. He had cuts and bruises on his hands, knees, and face. No more was he thinking of being a hero of the great biking hill. Our little, humbled “hero” of the hill was taken home to his mother, who sympathetically and lovingly washed and patched his wounds.

The next day Joey’s father returned home. When he saw the bandages on his son and the damaged bicycle, he guessed the story immediately. Joey’s bike was put away in storage for several weeks as punishment for his disobedience.

Joey sat on the curb as the boys raced down the hill, then on to the other street. Now Joey had no desire to sneak off and ride his bike with the big boys. He had learned his lesson—to always obey his father, even when he thought he knew better. He realized that his father was not trying to ruin his fun but instead he was trying to keep him safe.

When Joey was again allowed to ride his bike, he was quite content to ride peacefully around his little block of houses. From now on he was going to obey his father, not only in matters of safety, but in all things.

Enfants, obéissez à vos pères et à vos mères en toutes choses ; car cela est agréable au Seigneur. –Colossiens 3:20.

Il y a des années, un garçon nommé Joey vivait avec son père et sa mère à la périphérie d’une ville. Un jour, le père de Joey lui offrit un vélo tout neuf, rouge et blanc, qu’il désirait depuis longtemps.

Il y avait une grande colline près de leur maison où les grands garçons du quartier aimaient faire du vélo. Le père de Joey lui avait strictement interdit de faire du vélo avec eux sur la colline, car c’était trop dangereux. Il était seulement autorisé à rouler sur le joli trottoir lisse, à passer devant de nombreuses maisons, à traverser une petite ruelle, puis à revenir enfin chez lui.

Au fil des jours et des semaines, cela commença à perdre de son attrait. Il regardait avec envie les grands garçons pousser leurs vélos jusqu’en haut de la colline, presque juste devant sa maison. Arrivés au sommet, ils enfourchaient leurs vélos et, poussant des cris de joie, dévalaient la route goudronnée avant de tourner rapidement dans la rue adjacente, en bas de la colline.

« Youpi, nous voilà ! » criaient-ils en passant à toute vitesse, laissant Joey pédaler tranquillement autour de son petit pâté de maisons, encore et encore.

« Allez, Joey ! » criaient les garçons. « Pourquoi ne montes-tu pas avec nous ? Regarde comme on s’amuse ! Tu as trop peur », le taquinaient-ils.

Joey était trop gêné pour leur dire que son père le lui avait interdit parce qu’il était trop petit et risquait de tomber de son vélo et de se faire mal. Les garçons n’auraient fait que se moquer davantage de lui, alors il resta silencieux. Comme il aurait aimé pouvoir monter et montrer à ses amis qu’il n’avait pas peur ! Joey se dit : « Peut-être que si je descendais la colline une seule fois, mon père comprendrait que je ne suis plus si petit après tout. Alors papa serait fier de moi et me laisserait descendre la colline avec les grands garçons quand je le voudrais. Oh, comme ce serait excitant ! » Rien que d’y penser, son cœur se mit à battre rapidement d’impatience.

Joey n’eut pas à attendre longtemps avant d’en avoir l’occasion. Son père devait partir quelques jours pour affaires. Joey pensa que ce serait l’occasion de prouver à son père qu’il était capable de faire du vélo avec les grands garçons. Tout excité et impatient, il monta sa bicyclette jusqu’en haut de la colline. En compagnie des grands garçons, il se sentait tellement grand. Son père avait sûrement tort ! Il allait maintenant prouver à tout le monde qu’il savait mieux que quiconque ce qu’il était capable de faire ou non.

D’un élan et d’un bond, il se retrouva sur son vélo. À mesure que celui-ci allait de plus en plus vite, il agrippa le guidon plus fermement. À ce moment-là, l’un des garçons malicieux, qui montait la colline, lança une pierre sur le pneu de Joey tandis qu’il passait à toute vitesse. Joey fit brusquement un écart pour éviter la pierre. Avant même de comprendre ce qui se passait, il volait dans les airs sans son vélo. Il roula, glissa et rebondit avant de s’arrêter douloureusement. Joey était dans un piteux état. Son pantalon et sa chemise étaient déchirés. Il avait des coupures et des ecchymoses aux mains, aux genoux et au visage. Il ne pensait plus à devenir le héros de la grande colline des cyclistes. Notre petit « héros » humilié fut ramené chez lui auprès de sa mère, qui nettoya et pansa ses blessures avec compassion et affection.

Le lendemain, le père de Joey rentra à la maison. En voyant les bandages de son fils et le vélo endommagé, il devina aussitôt ce qui s’était passé. Le vélo de Joey fut rangé pendant plusieurs semaines, en punition de sa désobéissance.

Joey était assis sur le bord du trottoir tandis que les garçons dévalaient la colline, puis poursuivaient leur route dans l’autre rue. À présent, Joey n’avait plus envie de s’éclipser pour faire du vélo avec les grands garçons. Il avait retenu la leçon : toujours obéir à son père, même lorsqu’il pensait savoir mieux que lui. Il comprit que son père ne cherchait pas à gâcher son plaisir, mais plutôt à le protéger.

Quand Joey fut de nouveau autorisé à faire du vélo, il se contenta parfaitement de rouler tranquillement autour de son petit pâté de maisons. Désormais, il obéirait à son père, non seulement en matière de sécurité, mais en toutes choses.

Children, obey your parents in all things: for this is well pleasing unto the Lord –Col 3:20.

Years ago, there was a boy named Joey who lived with his father and mother on the outskirts of a city. One day Joey’s father gave him a brand new red and white bike, which he had been wanting for a long time.

There was a big hill close to their house where the big boys in the neighborhood enjoyed riding their bikes. Joey’s father strictly forbade him from riding with the big boys on the hill, since it was too dangerous. Instead, he was only allowed to ride down the nice smooth sidewalk, past numerous houses, through a little alley, and then finally back to his house once again.

As the days and weeks went by, this began to lose its excitement. He watched enviously as the big boys walked their bikes up the hill almost directly in front of his house. At the top they would jump on their bikes, and with gleeful shouts, race down the hardtop road, swiftly turning onto the adjoining street at the bottom of the hill.

“Whee, here we come!” they would shout as they rushed by, leaving Joey to pedal calmly on around his little block again and again.

“Come on Joey!” the boys hollered. “Why don’t you come up with us? See what fun we are having! You are too scared,” they teased.

Joey was too embarrassed to tell them that his father had forbidden him since he was too little and might fall off his bike and hurt himself. The boys would have only made more fun of him, so he remained silent. How he wished he could go up and show his friends that he was not afraid. Joey thought, “Maybe if I would go down the hill just once, my dad would realize that I’m not so little after all. Then Dad would be proud of me and let me go down the hill with the big boys anytime I want to. Oh, how exciting that would be.” The very thought made his heart beat quickly in anticipation.

Joey did not need to wait very long for his opportunity. His father was going to be gone for a couple of days on business. Joey thought this would be his chance to prove to his dad that he was able to ride his bike with the big boys. With excitement and anticipation, he took his bike up the hill. He felt so grown-up in the big boys’ company. Surely his father was wrong! Now he would prove to everybody that he knew better than anyone else what he was able to do and not do.

With a run and a hop, he was on his bike. As the bike went faster and faster, he grabbed the handlebars more firmly. At that moment, one of the mischievous boys, coming up the hill, tossed a stone at Joey’s tire as he flew by. Joey swerved sharply to avoid the stone. Before he knew what was happening, he was sailing thru the air without his bike. He rolled and skidded and bumped, before coming to a painful stop. Joey was one big mess. His pants and shirt were torn. He had cuts and bruises on his hands, knees, and face. No more was he thinking of being a hero of the great biking hill. Our little, humbled “hero” of the hill was taken home to his mother, who sympathetically and lovingly washed and patched his wounds.

The next day Joey’s father returned home. When he saw the bandages on his son and the damaged bicycle, he guessed the story immediately. Joey’s bike was put away in storage for several weeks as punishment for his disobedience.

Joey sat on the curb as the boys raced down the hill, then on to the other street. Now Joey had no desire to sneak off and ride his bike with the big boys. He had learned his lesson—to always obey his father, even when he thought he knew better. He realized that his father was not trying to ruin his fun but instead he was trying to keep him safe.

When Joey was again allowed to ride his bike, he was quite content to ride peacefully around his little block of houses. From now on he was going to obey his father, not only in matters of safety, but in all things.

Дети, будьте послушны родителям вашим во всем, ибо это благоугодно Господу. –Кол 3:20.

Много лет назад жил мальчик по имени Джоуи. Он жил с отцом и матерью на окраине города. Однажды отец подарил ему совершенно новый красно-белый велосипед, о котором он давно мечтал.

Недалеко от их дома был большой холм, где мальчики постарше из их района любили кататься на велосипедах. Отец Джоуи строго запретил ему кататься с ними на холме, потому что это было слишком опасно. Вместо этого ему разрешалось кататься только по ровному тротуару: мимо множества домов, через небольшой переулок и затем обратно домой.

Дни и недели шли, и это занятие стало терять свою привлекательность. Он с завистью наблюдал, как мальчики постарше ведут велосипеды вверх по холму почти прямо напротив его дома. На вершине они запрыгивали на велосипеды и, радостно крича, мчались вниз по твердой дороге, быстро сворачивая в примыкавшую к ней улицу у подножия холма.

«У-у-у, держитесь!» — кричали они, проносясь мимо, а Джоуи тем временем спокойно крутил педали вокруг своего квартала снова и снова.

«Давай, Джоуи!» — кричали мальчики. «Почему бы тебе не подняться с нами? Посмотри, как нам весело! Ты слишком трусишь», — дразнили они его.

Джоуи было слишком стыдно сказать им, что отец запретил ему кататься там, потому что он еще слишком мал и может упасть с велосипеда и ушибиться. Мальчики только стали бы дразнить его еще сильнее, поэтому он промолчал. Как ему хотелось подняться туда и показать друзьям, что он не боится. Джоуи подумал: «Может быть, если я всего один раз спущусь с холма, папа поймет, что я уже не такой маленький. Тогда папа будет мной гордиться и позволит мне кататься с мальчиками постарше с холма, когда я захочу. Ах, как здорово было бы!» От одной этой мысли сердце у него забилось быстрее от нетерпения.

Возможности Джоуи пришлось ждать недолго. Отцу нужно было уехать по делам на пару дней. Джоуи подумал, что это его шанс доказать отцу, что он уже способен кататься на велосипеде с мальчиками постарше. Взволнованный и полный предвкушения, он повел велосипед на холм. В компании мальчиков постарше он чувствовал себя таким взрослым. Наверняка отец ошибался! Теперь он докажет всем, что лучше кого бы то ни было знает, что ему по силам, а что нет.

Разбежавшись и подпрыгнув, он оказался на велосипеде. Чем быстрее ехал велосипед, тем крепче он сжимал руль. В этот момент один из озорных мальчиков, поднимавшихся на холм, бросил камень в колесо Джоуи, когда тот пролетал мимо. Джоуи резко свернул, чтобы увернуться от камня. Не успел он понять, что происходит, как уже летел по воздуху без велосипеда. Он перекатывался, скользил и ударялся, пока наконец не остановился, мучительно ушибленный. Джоуи был весь в синяках и ссадинах. Его брюки и рубашка были порваны. На руках, коленях и лице у него были порезы и синяки. Ему уже было не до того, чтобы считать себя героем великого велосипедного холма. Нашего маленького, смирившегося «героя» холма отвели домой к матери, и она с сочувствием и любовью промыла и перевязала его раны.

На следующий день отец Джоуи вернулся домой. Увидев бинты на сыне и поврежденный велосипед, он сразу догадался, что произошло. В наказание за непослушание велосипед Джоуи убрали на хранение на несколько недель.

Джоуи сидел на обочине, пока мальчики мчались вниз с холма, а затем ехали дальше по другой улице. Теперь у Джоуи не было ни малейшего желания тайком уехать и кататься на велосипеде с мальчиками постарше. Он усвоил урок: всегда слушаться отца, даже когда ему казалось, что он знает лучше. Он понял, что отец не пытался лишить его удовольствия, а, напротив, хотел уберечь его от опасности.

Когда Джоуи снова разрешили кататься на велосипеде, он вполне довольствовался тем, что спокойно ездил вокруг своего небольшого квартала. Отныне он собирался слушаться отца не только в вопросах безопасности, но во всем.

A princess of God!
It’s a calling sublime
That merits my giving
Of talent and time
To grow in the glory
Of what He would make--
My Father, the King,
Will all ugliness take
Away from my heart,
That it tarnish no more
And bring me the jewels
That He has in store.

A princess of God!
It’s a calling to live
A life that to others
Around me would give
A diamond of hope,
A desire for God,
The truth of salvation
By Jesus’ shed blood.
A call to live godly
In Jesus Christ,
Adorned with His meekness
And clothed with His light.

And he [Jesus] spake to them a parable; Behold the fig tree, and all the trees; When they now shoot forth, ye see and know of your own selves that summer is now nigh at hand. So likewise ye, when ye see these things come to pass, know ye that the kingdom of God is nigh at hand –Luk 21:29-31.

Summer truly is upon us; and the trees have shot forth. What an interesting term for our modern-day English language, yet we still understand its meaning and have a mental picture of what is happening—the leaves pushing out from places that over winter were bare. For me, I think it is easier to have this mental picture since I have seen time-lapse videos of plants growing or sprouting to life.

Anyway, so much for that. What about the rest of this verse? (…when ye see these things come to pass, know ye that the kingdom of God is nigh at hand.) Surely most of us continue to see the end of time approaching—the wars and rumors of wars, the earthquakes, the political upheaval in nation after nation, societies moving further and further away from God, and churches and families being ravished by sin and scandal.

We have God’s own promise that what we know and experience here on this earth was designed, created, and expected by Him to be only a temporary reality. And, Thou, Lord, in the beginning hast laid the foundation of the earth; and the heavens are the works of thine hands: They shall perish; but thou remainest; and they all shall wax old as doth a garment; And as a vesture shalt thou fold them up, and they shall be changed: but thou art the same, and thy years shall not fail –Heb 1:10-12.

The Prevailing Menace of Doubt & Fear

As we, as a church (FCF) and as a ministry (TBV), interact with numerous challenging situations (broken homes, struggling marriages, adopted children, faltering youth, immoral addictions, emotional struggles, and mental health issues) we repeatedly run into questions of doubt. “Why did this happen to me?” “Why doesn’t God change my circumstances?” “How can I trust God when all these painful things have happened to me?” “How can I surrender my life to God when He isn’t trustworthy?”

Most believers claim to trust God and believe His Word. The challenge that seems to come for each of us is two-fold. First, many of us tend to think that believing is primarily “feeling” instead of “choosing.” Secondly, many of us find it easy to believe what God says when it agrees with our experience, our thoughts, and our feelings; the problem arises when what the Scriptures say pushes on my will, my view, my belief, my experience, etc.

On the first point (believing=feeling) we have God’s clear answer from the Apostle Paul, for we walk by faith, not by sight: –2Co 5:7. On the second point the reality is that each of these struggles are a clear test of whether we will obey God rather than man (including ourselves), whether we will let God be true and every man a liar (including ourselves), and whether we will allow God to be the authority on all things or if we will still insist on our own will. Many of us claim (give lip service) to trust and believe God in all things, yet when we are faced with our own time of testing, we fail miserably (I know I have).

Additionally, many of us define our lifestyle of doubts and worry as being something normal, yet the Bible tells us to be anxious for nothing and to cast all our cares upon our Lord. Here the world has slowly deadened our senses to the clear teaching of the Scriptures, in that we have come to accept as normal that which God would have us to rise above. If we step back and consider the definition of “fear” as being on a spectrum, with some fear being quite minor and some being quite severe, we will see that many of our accepted patterns of behavior are outside of God’s perfect will for our lives. Doubt would be on the lesser end of the spectrum, with worry having a slightly stronger presence and effect, while panicking or being frantic would obviously cause much greater interference in our normal lives. Yet the truth is that each one of these is still in the family of “fear,” with the outcome being that we are allowing fear to control us and dictate our thoughts and behaviors. God’s will is that all His children would walk by faith instead of by fear.

God never gives us grace for any of our worries, nor for any future possible “what ifs”. God only gives us grace to go through what He is placing in front of us moment by moment. In the same way that a woman with child must go through the scary possibilities of the pain of childbirth, so likewise, all human beings must go through each circumstance that God decides is our lot in life. Nothing that we try to think or do (fear, worry, move, change our location, spend money, or ask others to intervene, etc.) will stop or change what God wills for our life. It is our choice to either accept or resist the inevitable in our lives.

The reality is this—each of us will either yield [our] members as instruments of unrighteousness unto sin by believing the lies of Satan and continuing to allow fear to motivate and direct our thoughts and actions, OR we will yield [ourself] unto God, as those that are alive from the dead, and our members as instruments of righteousness unto God (Rom 6:13), by choosing to believe what God says in His Word and allowing faith to motivate and direct our thoughts and actions.

Here a balancing perspective needs to be brought in. This does not mean that we never wrestle with difficult situations—Jesus did in the Garden of Gethsemane. It also doesn’t mean that we never appeal to God or our authorities to consider changing our current painful situation—again, Jesus did. Rather, we are to be honest with God (like Jesus was) about the struggle of our heart, but then we need to eventually walk forward in obedience, by faith, with courage (like Jesus did).

Ongoing Support Needed

A big thank you to all who so faithfully continue to support the work of The Berean Voice. It is through the many prayers, emails and phone calls of encouragement and suggestions, and the financial contributions of many believers that we can continue to minister to the needs of others. As a non-profit ministry of the church, we do not charge for our material or services, therefore we rely entirely on the ongoing freewill offerings of God’s people. Please prayerfully consider how God would have you to partner with us in this work.

If you believe that God would have you support us financially, monthly support makes our work easier since most of our bills are monthly. However, if this doesn’t work as well for you that is fine. For your convenience there is a remittance envelope in the center of each copy of the magazine or you can go to our website www.bereanvoice.org and use the “donate” feature there for online donations. E [Jesus] contou-lhes uma parábola: «Vede a figueira e todas as árvores. Quando começam a brotar, vós o vedes e sabeis por vós mesmos que o verão está agora próximo. Assim também vós, quando virdes estas coisas acontecerem, sabei que o reino de Deus está próximo» – Lc 21:29-31.

O verão realmente chegou, e as árvores brotaram. Que expressão interessante para o inglês moderno de hoje! Ainda assim, compreendemos o que significa e formamos uma imagem mental do que está acontecendo: as folhas surgindo de lugares que, durante o inverno, estavam despidos. Para mim, acho mais fácil formar essa imagem mental, pois já vi vídeos em time-lapse de plantas crescendo ou brotando para a vida.

Enfim, chega disso. E quanto ao restante deste versículo? (…quando virdes estas coisas acontecerem, sabei que o reino de Deus está próximo.) Certamente, a maioria de nós continua vendo o fim dos tempos se aproximar: guerras e rumores de guerras, terremotos, convulsões políticas em uma nação após outra, sociedades que se afastam cada vez mais de Deus, e igrejas e famílias devastadas pelo pecado e pelo escândalo.

Temos a própria promessa de Deus de que aquilo que conhecemos e vivenciamos aqui nesta terra foi concebido, criado e por Ele considerado apenas uma realidade temporária. E: Tu, Senhor, no principio fundaste a terra, e os céus são obra de tuas mãos: Elles perecerão, porém tu permanecerás; e todos elles, como roupa, se envelhecerão, E como uma manta os enrolarás, e mudar-se-hão, porém tu és o mesmo, e os teus annos não acabarão. – Hb 1:10-12.

A ameaça persistente da dúvida e do medo

Ao interagirmos, como igreja (FCF) e como ministério (TBV), com inúmeras situações desafiadoras (lares desfeitos, casamentos em dificuldades, crianças adotadas, jovens que fraquejam, vícios imorais, lutas emocionais e problemas de saúde mental), deparamos repetidamente com dúvidas. «Por que isso aconteceu comigo?» «Por que Deus não muda minhas circunstâncias?» «Como posso confiar em Deus quando todas essas coisas dolorosas aconteceram comigo?» «Como posso entregar minha vida a Deus quando Ele não é digno de confiança?»

A maioria dos crentes afirma confiar em Deus e acreditar em sua Palavra. O desafio que parece surgir para cada um de nós é duplo. Primeiro, muitos de nós tendem a pensar que acreditar é, antes de tudo, “sentir”, e não “escolher”. Em segundo lugar, muitos de nós acham fácil acreditar no que Deus diz quando isso concorda com nossa experiência, nossos pensamentos e nossos sentimentos; o problema surge quando aquilo que as Escrituras dizem confronta minha vontade, minha perspectiva, minha crença, minha experiência etc.

Quanto ao primeiro ponto (acreditar = sentir), temos a resposta clara de Deus por meio do apóstolo Paulo: porque andamos por fé, e não pelo que vemos – 2Co 5:7. Quanto ao segundo ponto, a realidade é que cada uma dessas lutas é um teste claro para saber se obedeceremos a Deus em vez de aos homens (inclusive a nós mesmos), se deixaremos Deus ser verdadeiro e todo homem mentiroso (inclusive nós mesmos), e se permitiremos que Deus seja a autoridade em todas as coisas ou se ainda insistiremos em fazer a nossa própria vontade. Muitos de nós afirmamos (dizemos da boca para fora) confiar em Deus e acreditar nele em todas as coisas, mas, quando enfrentamos nosso próprio período de provação, fracassamos miseravelmente (eu sei que já fracassei).

Além disso, muitos de nós definimos nosso estilo de vida de dúvidas e preocupações como algo normal, mas a Bíblia nos diz que não andemos ansiosos por coisa alguma e que lancemos sobre nosso Senhor todas as nossas ansiedades. Aqui, o mundo foi aos poucos entorpecendo nossos sentidos para o claro ensino das Escrituras, de modo que passamos a aceitar como normal aquilo que Deus deseja que superemos. Se pararmos para considerar a definição de “medo” como estando em um espectro, com alguns medos bastante leves e outros bastante graves, veremos que muitos dos padrões de comportamento que aceitamos estão fora da perfeita vontade de Deus para a nossa vida. A dúvida estaria na extremidade mais leve do espectro, a preocupação teria uma presença e um efeito um pouco mais fortes, enquanto entrar em pânico ou ficar em estado de agitação obviamente causaria uma interferência muito maior em nossa vida cotidiana. No entanto, a verdade é que cada um deles ainda pertence à categoria do “medo”, e o resultado é que estamos permitindo que o medo nos controle e dite nossos pensamentos e comportamentos. A vontade de Deus é que todos os seus filhos andem pela fé, e não pelo medo.

Deus nunca nos concede graça para qualquer uma de nossas preocupações, nem para quaisquer possíveis «e se» futuros. Deus só nos concede graça para passarmos pelo que Ele coloca diante de nós, momento a momento. Assim como uma mulher grávida precisa enfrentar as assustadoras possibilidades da dor do parto, também todos os seres humanos precisam passar por cada circunstância que Deus determina como nosso quinhão na vida. Nada do que tentemos pensar ou fazer (ter medo, preocupar-nos, mudar de lugar, mudar nossa localização, gastar dinheiro ou pedir a outros que intervenham etc.) impedirá ou mudará o que Deus quer para a nossa vida. A escolha é nossa: aceitar ou resistir ao inevitável em nossa vida.

A realidade é esta: cada um de nós entregará os [seus] membros ao pecado como instrumentos de injustiça, acreditando nas mentiras de Satanás e continuando a permitir que o medo motive e dirija nossos pensamentos e ações, OU se entregará a Deus, como quem reviveu dentre os mortos, e entregará os seus membros a Deus como instrumentos de justiça (Rm 6:13), escolhendo acreditar no que Deus diz em sua Palavra e permitindo que a fé motive e dirija nossos pensamentos e ações.

Aqui é necessário apresentar uma perspectiva equilibrada. Isso não significa que nunca lutamos com situações difíceis — Jesus lutou no jardim do Getsêmani. Também não significa que nunca apelamos a Deus ou às autoridades para que considerem mudar nossa situação dolorosa atual — mais uma vez, Jesus o fez. Pelo contrário, devemos ser honestos com Deus (como Jesus foi) sobre a luta em nosso coração, mas depois precisamos, finalmente, seguir em frente em obediência, pela fé e com coragem (como Jesus fez).

Necessidade contínua de apoio

Um grande agradecimento a todos os que continuam a apoiar fielmente o trabalho de The Berean Voice. É por meio das muitas orações, mensagens de e-mail e telefonemas de encorajamento e sugestões, e das contribuições financeiras de muitos crentes, que podemos continuar a atender às necessidades de outros. Como ministério sem fins lucrativos da igreja, não cobramos por nosso material ou serviços; por isso, dependemos inteiramente das ofertas voluntárias contínuas do povo de Deus. Por favor, considerem em oração como Deus gostaria que se unissem a nós neste trabalho.

Se acreditam que Deus deseja que nos apoiem financeiramente, o apoio mensal facilita nosso trabalho, já que a maioria das nossas contas é mensal. No entanto, se isso não for tão conveniente para vocês, não há problema. Para sua conveniência, há um envelope de remessa no centro de cada exemplar da revista; também podem acessar nosso site www.bereanvoice.org e usar a opção “doar” para fazer doações on-line. Abaixo está uma estimativa detalhada das nossas necessidades para sua consideração.

And he [Jesus] spake to them a parable; Behold the fig tree, and all the trees; When they now shoot forth, ye see and know of your own selves that summer is now nigh at hand. So likewise ye, when ye see these things come to pass, know ye that the kingdom of God is nigh at hand –Luk 21:29-31.

Summer truly is upon us; and the trees have shot forth. What an interesting term for our modern-day English language, yet we still understand its meaning and have a mental picture of what is happening—the leaves pushing out from places that over winter were bare. For me, I think it is easier to have this mental picture since I have seen time-lapse videos of plants growing or sprouting to life.

Anyway, so much for that. What about the rest of this verse? (…when ye see these things come to pass, know ye that the kingdom of God is nigh at hand.) Surely most of us continue to see the end of time approaching—the wars and rumors of wars, the earthquakes, the political upheaval in nation after nation, societies moving further and further away from God, and churches and families being ravished by sin and scandal.

We have God’s own promise that what we know and experience here on this earth was designed, created, and expected by Him to be only a temporary reality. And, Thou, Lord, in the beginning hast laid the foundation of the earth; and the heavens are the works of thine hands: They shall perish; but thou remainest; and they all shall wax old as doth a garment; And as a vesture shalt thou fold them up, and they shall be changed: but thou art the same, and thy years shall not fail –Heb 1:10-12.

The Prevailing Menace of Doubt & Fear

As we, as a church (FCF) and as a ministry (TBV), interact with numerous challenging situations (broken homes, struggling marriages, adopted children, faltering youth, immoral addictions, emotional struggles, and mental health issues) we repeatedly run into questions of doubt. “Why did this happen to me?” “Why doesn’t God change my circumstances?” “How can I trust God when all these painful things have happened to me?” “How can I surrender my life to God when He isn’t trustworthy?”

Most believers claim to trust God and believe His Word. The challenge that seems to come for each of us is two-fold. First, many of us tend to think that believing is primarily “feeling” instead of “choosing.” Secondly, many of us find it easy to believe what God says when it agrees with our experience, our thoughts, and our feelings; the problem arises when what the Scriptures say pushes on my will, my view, my belief, my experience, etc.

On the first point (believing=feeling) we have God’s clear answer from the Apostle Paul, for we walk by faith, not by sight: –2Co 5:7. On the second point the reality is that each of these struggles are a clear test of whether we will obey God rather than man (including ourselves), whether we will let God be true and every man a liar (including ourselves), and whether we will allow God to be the authority on all things or if we will still insist on our own will. Many of us claim (give lip service) to trust and believe God in all things, yet when we are faced with our own time of testing, we fail miserably (I know I have).

Additionally, many of us define our lifestyle of doubts and worry as being something normal, yet the Bible tells us to be anxious for nothing and to cast all our cares upon our Lord. Here the world has slowly deadened our senses to the clear teaching of the Scriptures, in that we have come to accept as normal that which God would have us to rise above. If we step back and consider the definition of “fear” as being on a spectrum, with some fear being quite minor and some being quite severe, we will see that many of our accepted patterns of behavior are outside of God’s perfect will for our lives. Doubt would be on the lesser end of the spectrum, with worry having a slightly stronger presence and effect, while panicking or being frantic would obviously cause much greater interference in our normal lives. Yet the truth is that each one of these is still in the family of “fear,” with the outcome being that we are allowing fear to control us and dictate our thoughts and behaviors. God’s will is that all His children would walk by faith instead of by fear.

God never gives us grace for any of our worries, nor for any future possible “what ifs”. God only gives us grace to go through what He is placing in front of us moment by moment. In the same way that a woman with child must go through the scary possibilities of the pain of childbirth, so likewise, all human beings must go through each circumstance that God decides is our lot in life. Nothing that we try to think or do (fear, worry, move, change our location, spend money, or ask others to intervene, etc.) will stop or change what God wills for our life. It is our choice to either accept or resist the inevitable in our lives.

The reality is this—each of us will either yield [our] members as instruments of unrighteousness unto sin by believing the lies of Satan and continuing to allow fear to motivate and direct our thoughts and actions, OR we will yield [ourself] unto God, as those that are alive from the dead, and our members as instruments of righteousness unto God (Rom 6:13), by choosing to believe what God says in His Word and allowing faith to motivate and direct our thoughts and actions.

Here a balancing perspective needs to be brought in. This does not mean that we never wrestle with difficult situations—Jesus did in the Garden of Gethsemane. It also doesn’t mean that we never appeal to God or our authorities to consider changing our current painful situation—again, Jesus did. Rather, we are to be honest with God (like Jesus was) about the struggle of our heart, but then we need to eventually walk forward in obedience, by faith, with courage (like Jesus did).

Ongoing Support Needed

A big thank you to all who so faithfully continue to support the work of The Berean Voice. It is through the many prayers, emails and phone calls of encouragement and suggestions, and the financial contributions of many believers that we can continue to minister to the needs of others. As a non-profit ministry of the church, we do not charge for our material or services, therefore we rely entirely on the ongoing freewill offerings of God’s people. Please prayerfully consider how God would have you to partner with us in this work.

If you believe that God would have you support us financially, monthly support makes our work easier since most of our bills are monthly. However, if this doesn’t work as well for you that is fine. Και τους είπε μια παραβολή: «Κοιτάξτε τη συκιά και όλα τα δέντρα· όταν αρχίζουν να βγάζουν φύλλα, βλέπετε και καταλαβαίνετε από μόνοι σας ότι το καλοκαίρι πλησιάζει. Έτσι κι εσείς, όταν δείτε να συμβαίνουν αυτά, να ξέρετε ότι η βασιλεία του Θεού πλησιάζει» –Λουκ. 21:29-31.

Το καλοκαίρι είναι πράγματι εδώ, και τα δέντρα έχουν βγάλει φύλλα. Τι ενδιαφέρουσα έκφραση για τη σύγχρονη αγγλική γλώσσα μας, κι όμως εξακολουθούμε να καταλαβαίνουμε το νόημά της και να σχηματίζουμε στο μυαλό μας μια εικόνα αυτού που συμβαίνει — τα φύλλα ξεπροβάλλουν από σημεία που όλο τον χειμώνα ήταν γυμνά. Νομίζω ότι για μένα είναι ευκολότερο να σχηματίσω αυτή την εικόνα, επειδή έχω δει βίντεο χρονικής παρέλευσης με φυτά να μεγαλώνουν ή να βλασταίνουν και να ζωντανεύουν.

Τέλος πάντων, αυτά προς το παρόν. Τι γίνεται με το υπόλοιπο εδάφιο; (…όταν δείτε να συμβαίνουν αυτά, να ξέρετε ότι η βασιλεία του Θεού πλησιάζει.) Σίγουρα οι περισσότεροι από εμάς εξακολουθούμε να βλέπουμε το τέλος του κόσμου να πλησιάζει — τους πολέμους και τις φήμες για πολέμους, τους σεισμούς, την πολιτική αναταραχή από το ένα έθνος στο άλλο, τις κοινωνίες να απομακρύνονται όλο και περισσότερο από τον Θεό, και εκκλησίες και οικογένειες να καταστρέφονται από την αμαρτία και τα σκάνδαλα.

Έχουμε τη δική Του υπόσχεση ότι όσα γνωρίζουμε και βιώνουμε εδώ στη γη σχεδιάστηκαν, δημιουργήθηκαν και προορίστηκαν από Εκείνον να είναι μόνο μια προσωρινή πραγματικότητα. καί· Συ κατ' αρχάς, Κύριε, την γην εθεμελίωσας, και έργα των χειρών σου είναι οι ουρανοί· αυτοί θέλουσιν απολεσθή, συ δε διαμένεις· και πάντες ως ιμάτιον θέλουσι παλαιωθή, και ως περιένδυμα θέλεις τυλίξει αυτούς, και θέλουσιν αλλαχθή· Συ όμως είσαι ο αυτός, και τα έτη σου δεν θέλουσιν εκλείψει –Προς Εβραίους 1:10-12.

Η Διαρκής Απειλή της Αμφιβολίας και του Φόβου

Καθώς εμείς, ως εκκλησία (FCF) και ως διακονία (TBV), αντιμετωπίζουμε πολλές δύσκολες καταστάσεις (διαλυμένα σπίτια, γάμους που δοκιμάζονται, υιοθετημένα παιδιά, νέους που παραπαίουν, ανήθικους εθισμούς, συναισθηματικές δυσκολίες και ζητήματα ψυχικής υγείας), ερχόμαστε επανειλημμένα αντιμέτωποι με ερωτήματα αμφιβολίας. «Γιατί μου συνέβη αυτό;» «Γιατί δεν αλλάζει ο Θεός τις συνθήκες μου;» «Πώς μπορώ να εμπιστεύομαι τον Θεό όταν μου έχουν συμβεί όλα αυτά τα οδυνηρά πράγματα;» «Πώς μπορώ να παραδώσω τη ζωή μου στον Θεό όταν δεν είναι άξιος εμπιστοσύνης;»

Οι περισσότεροι πιστοί ισχυρίζονται ότι εμπιστεύονται τον Θεό και πιστεύουν στον Λόγο Του. Η πρόκληση που φαίνεται να αντιμετωπίζουμε όλοι μας είναι διπλή. Πρώτον, πολλοί από εμάς τείνουμε να θεωρούμε ότι το να πιστεύουμε είναι κυρίως «να νιώθουμε» και όχι «να επιλέγουμε». Δεύτερον, πολλοί από εμάς βρίσκουμε εύκολο να πιστεύουμε όσα λέει ο Θεός όταν συμφωνούν με την εμπειρία, τις σκέψεις και τα αισθήματά μας· το πρόβλημα προκύπτει όταν όσα λένε οι Γραφές έρχονται σε σύγκρουση με τη θέλησή μου, την άποψή μου, την πεποίθησή μου, την εμπειρία μου κ.λπ.

Στο πρώτο σημείο (πίστη=συναίσθημα), έχουμε τη σαφή απάντηση του Θεού μέσω του αποστόλου Παύλου: γιατί περπατάμε με πίστη, όχι με την όραση –Β΄ Κορ. 5:7. Όσο για το δεύτερο σημείο, η πραγματικότητα είναι ότι καθεμία από αυτές τις δυσκολίες αποτελεί σαφή δοκιμασία για το αν θα υπακούσουμε στον Θεό αντί στους ανθρώπους (συμπεριλαμβανομένου του εαυτού μας), αν θα αφήσουμε τον Θεό να είναι αληθινός και κάθε άνθρωπο ψεύτη (συμπεριλαμβανομένου του εαυτού μας), και αν θα επιτρέψουμε στον Θεό να είναι η αυθεντία σε όλα ή αν θα επιμένουμε ακόμη στη δική μας θέληση. Πολλοί από εμάς ισχυριζόμαστε (λέμε απλώς λόγια) ότι εμπιστευόμαστε και πιστεύουμε στον Θεό για τα πάντα, κι όμως, όταν αντιμετωπίζουμε τη δική μας ώρα δοκιμασίας, αποτυγχάνουμε οικτρά (ξέρω ότι εγώ έχω αποτύχει).

Επιπλέον, πολλοί από εμάς θεωρούμε τον τρόπο ζωής που χαρακτηρίζεται από αμφιβολίες και ανησυχία κάτι φυσιολογικό, κι όμως η Βίβλος μάς λέει να μην ανησυχούμε για τίποτα και να ρίχνουμε όλες τις έγνοιες μας στον Κύριό μας. Εδώ ο κόσμος έχει σταδιακά αμβλύνει τις αισθήσεις μας απέναντι στη σαφή διδασκαλία των Γραφών, με αποτέλεσμα να έχουμε αποδεχτεί ως φυσιολογικό αυτό από το οποίο ο Θεός θέλει να υπερβούμε. Αν κάνουμε ένα βήμα πίσω και εξετάσουμε τον «φόβο» ως ένα φάσμα, όπου ορισμένοι φόβοι είναι πολύ ήπιοι και άλλοι πολύ έντονοι, θα δούμε ότι πολλά από τα μοτίβα συμπεριφοράς που έχουμε αποδεχτεί βρίσκονται έξω από το τέλειο θέλημα του Θεού για τη ζωή μας. Η αμφιβολία θα βρισκόταν στο πιο ήπιο άκρο του φάσματος, η ανησυχία θα είχε κάπως ισχυρότερη παρουσία και επίδραση, ενώ ο πανικός ή η ταραχή θα προκαλούσαν προφανώς πολύ μεγαλύτερη αναστάτωση στην καθημερινή μας ζωή. Η αλήθεια, ωστόσο, είναι ότι όλα αυτά εξακολουθούν να ανήκουν στην ίδια «οικογένεια» του φόβου, με αποτέλεσμα να επιτρέπουμε στον φόβο να μας ελέγχει και να υπαγορεύει τις σκέψεις και τις συμπεριφορές μας. Το θέλημα του Θεού είναι όλα τα παιδιά Του να περπατούν με πίστη αντί με φόβο.

Ο Θεός δεν μας δίνει ποτέ χάρη για καμία από τις ανησυχίες μας, ούτε για πιθανά μελλοντικά «κι αν». Ο Θεός μάς δίνει χάρη μόνο για να περάσουμε μέσα από όσα Εκείνος φέρνει μπροστά μας, στιγμή τη στιγμή. Όπως μια έγκυος γυναίκα πρέπει να περάσει τις τρομακτικές πιθανότητες του πόνου του τοκετού, έτσι και όλοι οι άνθρωποι πρέπει να περάσουμε κάθε περίσταση που ο Θεός αποφασίζει ότι είναι το μερίδιό μας στη ζωή. Τίποτε απ’ όσα προσπαθούμε να σκεφτούμε ή να κάνουμε (να φοβηθούμε, να ανησυχήσουμε, να μετακινηθούμε, να αλλάξουμε τόπο διαμονής, να ξοδέψουμε χρήματα ή να ζητήσουμε από άλλους να παρέμβουν κ.λπ.) δεν θα σταματήσει ούτε θα αλλάξει αυτό που θέλει ο Θεός για τη ζωή μας. Είναι δική μας επιλογή είτε να αποδεχτούμε είτε να αντισταθούμε στο αναπόφευκτο στη ζωή μας.

Η πραγματικότητα είναι η εξής: ο καθένας μας είτε παραδίδει τα μέλη του ως όπλα αδικίας στην αμαρτία, πιστεύοντας τα ψέματα του Σατανά και εξακολουθώντας να επιτρέπει στον φόβο να υποκινεί και να κατευθύνει τις σκέψεις και τις πράξεις του, ΕΙΤΕ παραδίδει τον εαυτό του στον Θεό, ως ζωντανός από τους νεκρούς, και τα μέλη του ως όπλα δικαιοσύνης στον Θεό (Ρωμ. 6:13), επιλέγοντας να πιστέψει όσα λέει ο Θεός στον Λόγο Του και επιτρέποντας στην πίστη να υποκινεί και να κατευθύνει τις σκέψεις και τις πράξεις του.

Εδώ χρειάζεται να προστεθεί μια εξισορροπητική οπτική. Αυτό δεν σημαίνει ότι δεν παλεύουμε ποτέ με δύσκολες καταστάσεις — ο Ιησούς πάλεψε στον κήπο της Γεθσημανή. Ούτε σημαίνει ότι δεν παρακαλούμε ποτέ τον Θεό ή τις αρχές μας να εξετάσουν το ενδεχόμενο να αλλάξει η τωρινή οδυνηρή μας κατάσταση — και πάλι, ο Ιησούς το έκανε. Αντίθετα, πρέπει να είμαστε ειλικρινείς με τον Θεό (όπως ήταν ο Ιησούς) για την πάλη της καρδιάς μας, αλλά ύστερα πρέπει τελικά να προχωρήσουμε με υπακοή, με πίστη και με θάρρος (όπως έκανε ο Ιησούς).

Χρειάζεται Συνεχής Υποστήριξη

Ένα μεγάλο ευχαριστώ σε όλους όσοι συνεχίζουν πιστά να στηρίζουν το έργο του The Berean Voice. Χάρη στις πολλές προσευχές, στα ενθαρρυντικά μηνύματα ηλεκτρονικού ταχυδρομείου και τηλεφωνήματα, στις προτάσεις, καθώς και στις οικονομικές συνεισφορές πολλών πιστών, μπορούμε να συνεχίζουμε να διακονούμε τις ανάγκες των άλλων. Ως μη κερδοσκοπική διακονία της εκκλησίας, δεν χρεώνουμε το υλικό ή τις υπηρεσίες μας· γι’ αυτό στηριζόμαστε εξ ολοκλήρου στις συνεχιζόμενες, εθελοντικές προσφορές του λαού του Θεού. Σας παρακαλούμε να εξετάσετε με προσευχή πώς θέλει ο Θεός να συνεργαστείτε μαζί μας σε αυτό το έργο.

Αν πιστεύετε ότι ο Θεός θέλει να μας στηρίξετε οικονομικά, η μηνιαία συνεισφορά διευκολύνει το έργο μας, καθώς οι περισσότεροι λογαριασμοί μας είναι μηνιαίοι. Ωστόσο, αν αυτό δεν σας εξυπηρετεί τόσο καλά, δεν πειράζει. Για τη διευκόλυνσή σας, υπάρχει ένας φάκελος αποστολής χρημάτων στο κέντρο κάθε τεύχους του περιοδικού ή μπορείτε να επισκεφτείτε τον ιστότοπό μας www.bereanvoice.org και να χρησιμοποιήσετε εκεί τη δυνατότητα «δωρεά» για ηλεκτρονικές δωρεές. Παρακάτω παρατίθεται μια κατά προσέγγιση ανάλυση των αναγκών μας, για να τη λάβετε υπόψη.

Nearly 43 years ago, on a warm August afternoon, two 19-year-olds (a young woman and her fiancé) excitedly came out of her parents’ home and walked slowly down a small hill toward a group of 200 waiting people. Her father, a minister, awaited them at the front of the aisle. Flushed with excitement they stood before him and listened to the short message he had prepared concerning marriage. Their hearts beating with anticipation they joyfully answered, “I do,” making a covenant with each other and with God.

They both understood what it meant to remain faithful “through sickness and health, poverty and wealth, for better or worse, till death do us part.” Generations before had shown them that it was possible. Parents and siblings had shown them. Uncles and aunts had shown them. This was going to be bliss into life’s sunset… Or so they thought.

It never entered their minds that great trials would test the very core of their belief and commitment. They went through hard financial times. (The balance in the checkbook was less than the bills that were due.) They went through times of life-changing decisions. (He wanted to quit his job working for his father-in-law building cabinets, receiving a regular paycheck, and begin farming with his father, which didn’t guarantee any income each week, let alone each year. She wasn’t so sure.) They had four children by this time and knew the challenge of crying babies and sleepless nights, which left everyone exhausted. They knew the differences that came up from time to time in church meetings that left them wondering which way they should think. (One brother thought one way and another thought differently, yet this couple respected both brothers.) Twelve years of experiences were behind them; still, married life was blissful and happy. Life’s sun was shining brightly!

Then it happened… The clouds began to roll in thick, angry waves! Eight years of misery and dysfunction were ahead. The devil was hard at work to destroy the unity and joy of these two whose marriage was going so beautifully. He allowed his heart and eyes to look at the allurements of the world and the deception of Satan. Her strong opinions and domineering attitude only added to the problem. Sparing the details, they lost the bliss they once enjoyed. It was a miserable existence for both of them. He was neither repentant nor asking forgiveness, but she continually forgave and pointed the children (five by now) to “we hate the sin, but we love our daddy.” After many years of broken oneness, her commitment to “whither thou goest, I will go” began a miracle. God’s grace was sufficient.

Why are they so happy now?

First, it must be said, it was the power of God working in both of their lives. God didn’t give up on them. He said He wouldn’t; and He didn’t. They were tempted but they didn’t go where Satan wanted them to go. They both have experienced the power of the Holy Spirit to bring them to depths of spiritual communion that they never knew before. It took many heart-wrenching prayers for strength and forgiveness. It took many deep, heartfelt tears of repentance and close accountability to each other. Many and much!

Secondly, as they look back to that time in their lives, there were four principles of God’s Word that were engrained so deeply into their minds that they couldn’t deny them:

  1. A covenant with God is powerful and cannot be broken.
  2. Unconditional love for another person is powerful.
  3. Real and ongoing personal repentance is powerful.
  4. Living a life (moment by moment) of forgiveness is powerful.

When those four God-ordained choices enter a war between the will of God and the wiles of the enemy, the enemy is powerless.

A covenant with God is undeniably unbreakable. When “the books are opened” the covenant will not have changed.

Unconditional love means loving even when it’s not so easy. Fires have a tendency to go out when they have cold water thrown on them. It requires a lot of staying really close to Jesus! Ann’s prayer and plea to God was “Lord, please draw Mark back to You by the power of Your Holy Spirit.” God answered!

When I, Mark, realized what I was losing, both in eternity and in this life with my family, and the depth and sinfulness of my sin, I trembled before God. He brought me to repentance. God began a healing that was exceeding and abundantly above all that Ann and I had ever thought or asked. My deep, heart-wrenching, grief-stricken repentance was real and obvious to her and the family. I took 100% of the blame. Everyone knows “there are always two sides to the story,” yet as the one who had committed the sin, I took full responsibility for my sin and the chaos that was brought into the marriage. I never blamed her for my sin. Humility is not difficult when it is heartfelt and Holy Spirit-guided!

My, Ann’s response to Mark’s repentance was full and free forgiveness. His ongoing expression of repentance and the fact that he took all the blame was powerful in rebuilding trust. It was clear that God was blessing our marriage again! The sun was shining through clouds that were rapidly receding!

Today, 23 years later, photos of that season in our lives or some reminiscent moment is apt to wash up fresh tears of grief and repentance for the pain and wasted years. Ongoing repentance and ready forgiveness have proven beautiful in building trust and a relationship that is sweeter and stronger than ever before! God truly has fulfilled His promise to … restore to [us] the years that the locust hath eaten! (Joel 2:25a) Praise the Lord!

كان كلاهما يفهم معنى الأمانة «في المرض والصحة، في الفقر والغنى، في السراء والضراء، إلى أن يفرقنا الموت». وقد أظهرت لهما أجيال سبقت أنه أمر ممكن. أراهما ذلك والداهما وإخوتهما وأخواتهما، وأعمامهما وعماتهما وأخوالهما وخالاتهما. وظنا أن حياتهما ستكون نعيمًا حتى مغيب شمس العمر… أو هكذا اعتقدا.

لم يخطر ببالهما قط أن محنًا عظيمة ستختبر صميم إيمانهما والتزامهما. مرا بأوقات مالية عصيبة. (كان رصيد دفتر الشيكات أقل من الفواتير المستحقة.) ومرا بأوقات فرضت عليهما قرارات تغيّر مجرى الحياة. (أراد هو أن يترك عمله لدى حميه في صناعة الخزائن، حيث كان يتقاضى راتبًا منتظمًا، وأن يبدأ الزراعة مع أبيه، وهو عمل لا يضمن أي دخل كل أسبوع، فضلًا عن كل سنة. أما هي فلم تكن واثقة من ذلك.) كان لديهما آنذاك أربعة أطفال، وعرفا تحدي بكاء الرضع والليالي التي لا نوم فيها، مما كان يترك الجميع منهكين. وعرفا الاختلافات التي كانت تظهر من وقت إلى آخر في اجتماعات الكنيسة، فتتركهما يتساءلان أي رأي ينبغي أن يتبنيا. (كان أحد الإخوة يرى الأمر على نحو، ويراه آخر على نحو مختلف، ومع ذلك احترم الزوجان كلا الأخوين.) مضت اثنتا عشرة سنة من الخبرات؛ ومع ذلك كانت الحياة الزوجية نعيمًا وسعادة. كانت شمس الحياة تشرق ساطعة!

ثم حدث ذلك… وبدأت الغيوم تتكاثف وتندفع في موجات هائجة! وكانت أمامهما ثماني سنوات من البؤس والاضطراب. كان إبليس يعمل جاهدًا على تدمير الوحدة والفرح اللذين نعمت بهما حياة هذين الزوجين. فقد سمح هو لقلبه وعينيه بالانجذاب إلى مغريات العالم وخداع الشيطان. ولم تضف آراؤها القوية وموقفها المتسلط إلا إلى المشكلة. ومن دون الخوض في التفاصيل، فقدا النعيم الذي تمتعا به من قبل. وكانت حياة كلٍّ منهما بائسة. لم يكن هو تائبًا ولا طالبًا للمغفرة، لكنها كانت تسامحه باستمرار وتعلّم الأطفال (وقد صاروا خمسة) أن «نحن نكره الخطية، لكننا نحب أبانا». وبعد سنوات عديدة من انكسار وحدتهما، بدأ التزامها بقولها «حيثما تذهب أذهب» معجزةً. كانت نعمة الله كافية.

لماذا يعيشان الآن بهذه السعادة؟

أولًا، لا بد من القول إن ما حدث كان بفعل قوة الله العاملة في حياة كليهما. لم يتخلَّ الله عنهما. قال إنه لن يفعل؛ ولم يفعل. تعرضا للتجربة، لكنهما لم يسلكا الطريق الذي أراد الشيطان لهما أن يسلكاه. وقد اختبر كلاهما قوة الروح القدس، إذ قادهما إلى أعماق من الشركة الروحية لم يعرفاها من قبل. تطلب الأمر صلوات كثيرة موجعة للقلب طلبًا للقوة والمغفرة. وتطلب دموعًا كثيرة عميقة صادقة نابعة من القلب، وتوبةً ومحاسبةً متبادلةً وثيقة. الكثير والكثير!

ثانيًا، عندما ينظران إلى الوراء إلى تلك الفترة من حياتهما، يجدان أن مبادئ أربعة من كلمة الله ترسخت في ذهنيهما بعمق، حتى لم يستطيعا إنكارها:

  1. العهد مع الله قوي ولا يمكن نقضه.
  2. المحبة غير المشروطة لشخص آخر قوية.
  3. التوبة الشخصية الحقيقية والمستمرة قوية.
  4. أن يعيش المرء حياةً قوامها (لحظةً بلحظة) المسامحة أمر قوي.

عندما تدخل هذه الخيارات الأربعة التي رسمها الله في صراع بين مشيئة الله ومكايد العدو، يصبح العدو عاجزًا.

العهد مع الله لا يمكن نقضه قطعًا. فعندما «تُفتح الأسفار»، لن يكون العهد قد تغيّر.

تعني المحبة غير المشروطة أن تحب حتى عندما لا يكون الأمر سهلًا. فالنار تميل إلى الانطفاء عندما يُسكب عليها ماء بارد. ويتطلب الأمر ملازمة يسوع عن قرب! وكان دعاء آن وتوسلها إلى الله: «يا رب، أرجوك أن تردّ مارك إليك بقوة روحك القدوس». وقد استجاب الله!

حين أدركتُ أنا، مارك، ما كنت أخسره، سواء في الأبدية أو في هذه الحياة مع عائلتي، وأدركت عمق خطيتي وشرّها، ارتعدت أمام الله. وقد قادني إلى التوبة. وبدأ الله شفاءً يفوق كل ما فكرنا فيه أو طلبناه أنا وآن، وفوق ذلك بكثير. كانت توبتي العميقة، الموجعة للقلب، المثقلة بالحزن حقيقيةً وواضحةً لها وللعائلة. تحملتُ المسؤولية كاملةً، بنسبة 100%. والجميع يعرف أن «للقصة دائمًا وجهين»، لكنني، بصفتي من ارتكب الخطية، تحملت المسؤولية كاملة عن خطيتي وعن الفوضى التي جلبتها إلى الزواج. ولم ألقِ عليها قط مسؤولية خطيتي. لا تكون الاتضاع صعبًا حين يكون نابعًا من القلب وبتوجيه الروح القدس!

أما أنا، آن، فكان ردي على توبة مارك مسامحةً كاملةً وحرة. وكان تعبيره المستمر عن توبته، وتحمله كامل اللوم، عاملًا قويًا في إعادة بناء الثقة. وقد اتضح أن الله يبارك زواجنا من جديد! كانت الشمس تشرق عبر الغيوم التي أخذت تنقشع سريعًا!

واليوم، بعد 23 عامًا، كثيرًا ما تثير صور تلك المرحلة من حياتنا، أو لحظة تذكّرنا بها، دموعًا جديدة من الحزن والتوبة بسبب الألم والسنوات الضائعة. وقد ثبت أن التوبة المستمرة والمسامحة المستعدة أمران جميلان في بناء الثقة وعلاقة صارت أحلى وأقوى من أي وقت مضى! لقد تمّم الله حقًا وعده بأن «يردّ لنا السنين التي أكلها الجراد»! (يوئيل 2:25أ) فليُسبَّح الرب!

And he [Jesus] spake to them a parable; Behold the fig tree, and all the trees; When they now shoot forth, ye see and know of your own selves that summer is now nigh at hand. So likewise ye, when ye see these things come to pass, know ye that the kingdom of God is nigh at hand –Luk 21:29-31.

Summer truly is upon us; and the trees have shot forth. What an interesting term for our modern-day English language, yet we still understand its meaning and have a mental picture of what is happening—the leaves pushing out from places that over winter were bare. For me, I think it is easier to have this mental picture since I have seen time-lapse videos of plants growing or sprouting to life.

Anyway, so much for that. What about the rest of this verse? (…when ye see these things come to pass, know ye that the kingdom of God is nigh at hand.) Surely most of us continue to see the end of time approaching—the wars and rumors of wars, the earthquakes, the political upheaval in nation after nation, societies moving further and further away from God, and churches and families being ravished by sin and scandal.

We have God’s own promise that what we know and experience here on this earth was designed, created, and expected by Him to be only a temporary reality. And, Thou, Lord, in the beginning hast laid the foundation of the earth; and the heavens are the works of thine hands: They shall perish; but thou remainest; and they all shall wax old as doth a garment; And as a vesture shalt thou fold them up, and they shall be changed: but thou art the same, and thy years shall not fail –Heb 1:10-12.

The Prevailing Menace of Doubt & Fear

As we, as a church (FCF) and as a ministry (TBV), interact with numerous challenging situations (broken homes, struggling marriages, adopted children, faltering youth, immoral addictions, emotional struggles, and mental health issues) we repeatedly run into questions of doubt. “Why did this happen to me?” “Why doesn’t God change my circumstances?” “How can I trust God when all these painful things have happened to me?” “How can I surrender my life to God when He isn’t trustworthy?”

Most believers claim to trust God and believe His Word. The challenge that seems to come for each of us is two-fold. First, many of us tend to think that believing is primarily “feeling” instead of “choosing.” Secondly, many of us find it easy to believe what God says when it agrees with our experience, our thoughts, and our feelings; the problem arises when what the Scriptures say pushes on my will, my view, my belief, my experience, etc.

On the first point (believing=feeling) we have God’s clear answer from the Apostle Paul, for we walk by faith, not by sight: –2Co 5:7. On the second point the reality is that each of these struggles are a clear test of whether we will obey God rather than man (including ourselves), whether we will let God be true and every man a liar (including ourselves), and whether we will allow God to be the authority on all things or if we will still insist on our own will. Many of us claim (give lip service) to trust and believe God in all things, yet when we are faced with our own time of testing, we fail miserably (I know I have).

Additionally, many of us define our lifestyle of doubts and worry as being something normal, yet the Bible tells us to be anxious for nothing and to cast all our cares upon our Lord. Here the world has slowly deadened our senses to the clear teaching of the Scriptures, in that we have come to accept as normal that which God would have us to rise above. If we step back and consider the definition of “fear” as being on a spectrum, with some fear being quite minor and some being quite severe, we will see that many of our accepted patterns of behavior are outside of God’s perfect will for our lives. Doubt would be on the lesser end of the spectrum, with worry having a slightly stronger presence and effect, while panicking or being frantic would obviously cause much greater interference in our normal lives. Yet the truth is that each one of these is still in the family of “fear,” with the outcome being that we are allowing fear to control us and dictate our thoughts and behaviors. God’s will is that all His children would walk by faith instead of by fear.

God never gives us grace for any of our worries, nor for any future possible “what ifs”. God only gives us grace to go through what He is placing in front of us moment by moment. In the same way that a woman with child must go through the scary possibilities of the pain of childbirth, so likewise, all human beings must go through each circumstance that God decides is our lot in life. Nothing that we try to think or do (fear, worry, move, change our location, spend money, or ask others to intervene, etc.) will stop or change what God wills for our life. It is our choice to either accept or resist the inevitable in our lives.

The reality is this—each of us will either yield [our] members as instruments of unrighteousness unto sin by believing the lies of Satan and continuing to allow fear to motivate and direct our thoughts and actions, OR we will yield [ourself] unto God, as those that are alive from the dead, and our members as instruments of righteousness unto God (Rom 6:13), by choosing to believe what God says in His Word and allowing faith to motivate and direct our thoughts and actions.

Here a balancing perspective needs to be brought in. This does not mean that we never wrestle with difficult situations—Jesus did in the Garden of Gethsemane. It also doesn’t mean that we never appeal to God or our authorities to consider changing our current painful situation—again, Jesus did. Rather, we are to be honest with God (like Jesus was) about the struggle of our heart, but then we need to eventually walk forward in obedience, by faith, with courage (like Jesus did).

Ongoing Support Needed

A big thank you to all who so faithfully continue to support the work of The Berean Voice. It is through the many prayers, emails and phone calls of encouragement and suggestions, and the financial contributions of many believers that we can continue to minister to the needs of others. As a non-profit ministry of the church, we do not charge for our material or services, therefore we rely entirely on the ongoing freewill offerings of God’s people. Please prayerfully consider how God would have you to partner with us in this work.

If you believe that God would have you support us financially, monthly support makes our work easier since most of our bills are monthly. However, if this doesn’t work as well for you that is fine. For your convenience there is a remittance envelope in the center of each copy of the magazine or you can go to our website www.bereanvoice.org and use the “donate” feature there for online donations.
